text:
jonathan: FYI - seeing NaNs/inf in outputs from the fusion-v2 fused-attn kernel when running 8-bit quantized models with KV cache reuse and mixed batching (short+long). Repro on prod-sim, high P99 spikes.

kai: can you paste the minimal repro + model + seq len distribution?

jonathan: repro outline: run with --kernel fusion-v2 --quant fp8 --kv-reuse true --batching heuristic_mixed. Example command:
```
./run_infer --model redwood/llama-7b-q8 --kernel fusion-v2 --seq-len 2048 --batching heuristic_mixed --batch-config "8x64,2x2048"
```
Logs snippet: 
```
EPOCH 0: softmax overflow at step 42 -> inf token probs
stack: aten::softmax -> fused_attn_cuda.cu:452
qk_max=4.7e+2 qk_min=-3.2e+2
```

siva: profiler shows fusion-v2 gives ~3.6x throughput vs flash-v3 but ~12% failure-rate for this mixed-batch testcase when kv cache is warm. p99 latency jumps by ~250ms on affected microbatches. Flame graph uploaded: https://ci.internal/redwood/flame/1967532100

maria: quick local experiments: switching to bf16 kernel (fusion-v2-bf16) resolves NaNs. Also tried flash-v3 (non-fused) with fp8 and it stayed numerically stable — it does a per-row renorm before exp which helps.

jonathan: hypothesis: fp8 + KV reuse + mixed short/long batches produce large variance in q·k accumulators. softmax exponent sees huge values -> overflow. batching heuristic folds short seqs into same kernel launch as long ones so internal scaling assumptions break.

kai: two-pronged mitigation proposal: 1) kernel-selector rule: prefer flash-v3 (or bf16 variant) when quant=fp8 && kv_reuse=true && batch_mix=short_long; 2) add softmax stabilization/clamping in fusion-v2: subtract max per row (we already do this in theory) and clamp exp input to reasonable range (e.g., [-50, 50]).

siva: quick clamp patch applied to local build: clamp_exp(x) = min(max(x, -50.0f), 50.0f). Microbench results: failure-rate down from 12% -> 0.2%, p99 latency still +8% vs baseline fused (but acceptable). Patch diff: https://git.internal/r/patches/4521

maria: we should avoid blanket clamping for all runs — only when quant=fp8 or when qk magnitude variance exceeds threshold. Otherwise we lose perf advantage for normal workloads.

jonathan: agreed. also add a telemetry counter for "softmax_clamp_applied" and "kernel_fallback_reason=fp8_kv_mixed". This will let us A/B safely.

perf-ci: nightly perf run summary: fusion-v2 (fp8) throughput +2.9x, NaN_count=122 on test-corpus A. With clamp patch NaN_count=1, throughput delta -8%. See artifacts: https://ci.internal/results/1967532100

maria: propose canary rollout plan: 5% traffic on dedicated clusters with telemetry gating (NaN_count threshold + p99 regressions). If metrics good after 24h, increase.

engbot: deploy scheduled: canary rollout (5%) on 2026-03-18T03:00Z. Automated rollback if NaN_count > 10 or p99 regression > 20% over baseline. :rocket:

jonathan: created issue #4521 (attn-kernel-numeric-spillover) and opened PR with selector heuristics + guarded clamp. @kai can you review the selector changes? tagging for follow-up. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
